brief: Iran's drones hit Kuwait while Washington tells citizens to *leave Iran*.
The ELN killed a woman it kidnapped in August; Colombia's president promises a *response*.
EU leaders fight over a *record budget* and a loan for Ukraine.
Ebola in Congo passes *12,000* confirmed cases.
Argentina is officially in a *technical recession*.

items.title: ELN kidnap victim Anyi Jácome found dead in Norte de Santander
items.summary:
Campesinos found a body on a roadside in rural Ábrego, Norte de Santander, on Thursday, 26 November. Relatives identified it as Anyi Jácome, who was kidnapped by the ELN on 16 August (the Defensoría places it a day later) along with three police officers on the road between Cúcuta and Ocaña. Medicina Legal still has to confirm identity and cause of death. President Abelardo de la Espriella called the killing a crime that "will not go unpunished", ordered troops and police to Catatumbo and demanded the release of the three officers still held.

The ELN claimed the abduction and said the officers had links to a FARC dissident front, and it made accusations against Jácome. Her family, a mother of a four-year-old girl, rejects them and says she belonged to no armed group. The Defensoría del Pueblo condemned the killing and asked for the officers' immediate, unconditional release. Watch for the forensic result and whether the officers are freed.

items.title: Minimum wage talks move forward after productivity data
items.summary:
On Thursday, 26 November, the government, business groups and unions met for the first session on productivity, the figure that feeds into the 2027 minimum wage. DANE's preliminary third-quarter data show labour productivity per hour worked up 2.24%, while productivity per employed person fell 0.98%. Labour Minister Natalia López Fuentes said the meeting was not about percentages, only about agreeing the productivity base.

The unions' central, the CUT, says it will present a wage proposal on 10 December. The raise usually decides how much a worker's pay and many prices (rent, fees, some services) will change next year, so it matters to freelancers too. Earlier reports mention 15 December as the first deadline for a deal.

items.title: Thanksgiving storms flood both US coasts and knock out power
items.summary:
Storms hit the East and West coasts on Thanksgiving, Thursday 26 November. More than 600,000 homes and businesses lost power by the afternoon, mostly on the East Coast. All of New Jersey was under a state of emergency, with some of the worst flooding in memory in towns like Avalon. Macy's postponed its Manhattan parade until Saturday because of wind. On the West Coast, king tides and waves tore down part of a pier in Pacifica, California.

The National Weather Service warned of airport disruption in the east through Friday morning, and coastal flood warnings remain on the West Coast. Heavy snow was also forecast around St. Louis, with up to 33 cm.

items.title: Argentina enters a technical recession
items.summary:
Argentina's economy shrank 1.8% between July and September, after a 1% fall in the second quarter, according to the Indec activity indicator. Two straight quarterly drops are the usual definition of a technical recession. Consumption is weak, personal loans cost about 64% a year, unemployment hit 7.9% in the second quarter, and inflation is forecast near 31% for 2026. The government has asked for caution before using the word recession; economists say the data are clear.

President Javier Milei's earlier gains, such as lower inflation than in 2023 and a fiscal surplus, still stand, but the recovery he promised is not showing up in daily life. Final GDP figures are due on 16 December.

items.title: EU leaders clash over a record budget and a loan for Ukraine
items.summary:
EU leaders met in Brussels on 26 November to argue over the 2028-2034 budget. Council President António Costa has proposed cutting the original plan by €204 billion, and nobody is happy. Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, the Netherlands, Sweden and Germany want deeper cuts to farm and cohesion funds. A group of 17 mostly southern and eastern states wants to protect them. Separately, the Commission proposes a €45 billion loan to cover about two-thirds of a €70 billion gap in Ukraine's 2027 budget. Slovakia, Czechia, Hungary and Bulgaria do not want to take part, though Bulgaria now says it is ready to join.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has threatened to veto the budget unless all 27 states agree on Ukraine support. Slovak PM Robert Fico calls that blackmail. A final deal is aimed for December, and delays could collide with France's 2027 presidential election.

items.title: Russia fires missiles and drones at Ukraine; Kyiv hits Russian energy sites
items.summary:
Russia hit Ukraine with ballistic missiles and 113 drones overnight into Thursday, 26 November. Ukraine's air defence shot down or neutralised 87 targets. At least three people were killed in Kharkiv, and seven were wounded in Kyiv. Ukrainian drones hit a power plant and a chemical plant in Stavropol, the Kuibyshev refinery in Samara and a pipeline station in Bashkortostan. Russia's Defence Ministry says it destroyed 343 Ukrainian drones; Euronews could not verify that figure.

Both sides now strike each other's energy and industry as winter begins. Separately, the two countries swapped war dead: 250 bodies to Ukraine and 22 to Russia, according to RBC citing a Russian lawmaker. The Kremlin has not committed to broad peace talks.

items.title: Eurozone leaders back Spain's Hernández de Cos to lead the ECB
items.summary:
Eurozone leaders gave majority support on 26 November to Pablo Hernández de Cos, 55, head of the Bank for International Settlements, to succeed Christine Lagarde as president of the European Central Bank. He would be the first Spaniard in the job. Lagarde said on 29 October she will leave on 7 February 2027.

The formal appointment is expected in December. Economists quoted by Euronews see him as a pragmatic centrist who will broadly keep Lagarde's course. The ECB sets interest rates for the euro, which affects loans and prices across Europe.

items.title: Iranian drones hit Kuwait as the US tells citizens to leave Iran
items.summary:
Kuwait's military said "a number of hostile" Iranian drones were intercepted on Thursday, 26 November, and that falling debris injured four people. Italy's foreign ministry said two Italians working for German defence firm Rheinmetall died. Kuwait's defence ministry blamed Iran. Iran's embassy in Rome "categorically" rejected responsibility and blamed US and Israeli aggression. Flights between Europe, the Gulf and Asia were rerouted around Kuwaiti airspace.

On 25 November the US Virtual Embassy in Iran told American citizens to leave Iran immediately, warning that hostilities could escalate fast. It said Iran attacked US assets in Bahrain and Kuwait, and that a Houthi strike on a Riyadh tower wounded 11 people, per Saudi Civil Defence. The war began in late February 2026. The US and Iran are also in a standoff over the Strait of Hormuz, a key oil route. Watch for more Gulf attacks and for Qatar's effort to revive talks.

items.title: Ebola in Congo passes 12,000 confirmed cases
items.summary:
Congo's health ministry reports 12,021 confirmed Ebola cases in the east of the country, nearly half of them fatal. Euronews, citing AP, calls it the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history and the deadliest of Congo's 17. It is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, which has no approved vaccine or treatment, and was declared in May. The 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak killed about 11,000 people.

Fighting between the army and rebels near Bunia, in Ituri province, has blocked teams from some communities, according to the WHO. The WHO backed trials of two new vaccines in November. Watch for whether the fighting eases and whether the trials show results.

feature.title: Russia and Ukraine: the war in five steps
steps: How it began: Ukraine became independent in 1991. In 2014, after protests ousted a pro-Russian president, Russia took Crimea and backed separatists in the east, in Donetsk and Luhansk.

Turning points: On 24 February 2022 Russia launched a full-scale invasion. Ukraine pushed Russian forces back from Kyiv and later retook territory around Kharkiv and Kherson. After that the front line slowed into a long war of attrition.

Where it stands: The war continues. Russia fires missiles and drones at Ukrainian cities, and Ukraine strikes Russian refineries and power plants. The two sides still swap war dead, but the Kremlin has not committed to broad peace talks. Ukraine faces a €70 billion gap in its 2027 budget.

What each side wants: Moscow says it wants security guarantees and control of the territory it claims. Kyiv wants Russian forces out, its borders restored and firm guarantees against a new attack. European governments are split on how much to pay.
What to watch: The EU's €45 billion Ukraine loan and the budget fight, whether the Kremlin accepts real talks, and attacks on energy infrastructure this winter.
